headline: Genomic and gene-level models link microbial genes and plasmids to hosts and disease
label: Microbiome Genomics And Functional Modeling
summary: Large genome and gene-level datasets are being paired with computational models to infer plasmid hosts, host sex, and functional typing in microbiomes.
synthesis: The common thread is pairing large genomic or gene-level data from shotgun metagenomes and genome collections with computational models to infer host and functional effects. CUPID extends nanopore methylation-based plasmid-host linking from MAGs to contigs and reads, assigning carbapenemase plasmids to hosts in mock and patient samples. SCiMS infers host chromosomal sex from host-derived reads in shotgun metagenomes at low host coverage. Cassette2Vec-EC encodes genomic-island gene neighborhoods as fixed-length vectors and uses genome-grouped machine learning with SHAP to predict pathogenic E. cecorum lineages. A global atlas of over 4,000 Bifidobacterium longum and B. infantis genomes from 48 countries guides infant probiotic design, while gene-level bimodality across natural microbial communities supports gene-based functional typing, with gut genes predictive of disease. The set is heterogeneous; the shared pattern is the coupling of genome-scale data with inference models rather than a single shared method.
